Field.name: InputImageFile
Field.usage: Input image file with images to be normalized or with exposure data
Field.manpage: Input file with images to be normalized, or whose header contains the exposure data needed for scaling. This entry is optional unless an output image file is entered. If the option is not entered and there is a non-option argument, the latter will be used as the input file.

Field.name: OutputImageFile
Field.usage: Output file for normalized images
Field.manpage: Output file for normalized images. If this option is not entered, the second non-option argument will be used for this output file.

Field.name: WeightOutputFile
Field.usage: Output file with weighting factors (optional)
Field.manpage: Output file with weighting factors that can be supplied to Tilt(1), which can be either relative factors with a mean of 1 or factors that would convert each image to transmittances.

Field.name: ImagesWithExposures
Field.usage: Image file with exposure information in header
Field.manpage: Image file with exposure information in header. Use this option to specify a raw stack if the images to be normalized no longer have exposure data in their header, such as would occur with montages.

Field.name: ReferenceImageFile
Field.usage: File with a reference image of the blank beam
Field.manpage: File with a reference image of the blank beam. If the mean value and the exposure for a reference image is known, then the exposure value for each image can be used to scale the data to transmittances.

Field.name: MeanOfReferenceImage
Field.usage: Mean value of a reference image for absolute normalization
Field.manpage: Mean value of a reference image, which can be used for absolute normalization to transmittances. This option and the reference image file cannot both be entered.

Field.name: ExposureOfReferenceImage
Field.usage: Exposure time or electron dose for a reference image
Field.manpage: Exposure time or electron dose of a reference image, which can be combined with the exposure values for each view to achieve absolute normalization. If this option is entered together with a reference image file, the given value supercedes the exposure value in the header of the reference image, if any.

Field.name: SubtractedIntegers
Field.usage: 32768 was subtracted from the data before storing as signed integers
Field.manpage: One of the ways of storing data from a 16-bit camera into the signed integer mode, 1, is to subtract 32768. Use this option to indicate that this occurred, and to have 32768 added back before normalization.

Field.name: Resubtract
Field.usage: Subtract 32768 off again after normalizing subtracted integers
Field.manpage: Subtract 32768 off again after normalizing subtracted integers.

Field.name: DivideBy2
Field.usage: Divide by 2 after normalizing subtracted integers
Field.manpage: Divide by 2 after normalizing subtracted integers. This option and -resubtract are relevant only if the data were subtracted integers, a relative normalization is being done, the mode of the output file is 1, and logs are not being taken. If there are values above 0 in the input file, one or the other option is needed to avoid truncating these values.

Field.name: LogOfOutput
Field.usage: Take log of output values after adding the given value
Field.manpage: Take log of output values after adding the given value. If the data have had 32768 subtracted from them, and you are just taking the log, you can enter "-log 32768" without using the -subtracted option, or "-log 0" with the -subtracted option.

Field.name: ModeOfOutput
Field.usage: Mode of output file: 0 byte, 1/6 signed/unsigned integer, 2 or 12 float
Field.manpage: Mode of output file: 0 for bytes (almost certainly useless), 1 for signed 16-bit integers, 6 for unsigned 16-bit integers, 2 for floating point numbers, or 12 for 16-bit floats. The default is to use the mode of the input file, although the default mode of floating point output for MRC files is governed by the value of environment variable IMOD_WRITE_FLOATS_16BIT. Mode 12 is allowed only if the output format is MRC.

Field.name: ScalingFactor
Field.usage: Factor for scaling the output after normalizing and taking log
Field.manpage: Factor for scaling the output after data are normalized and the log is taken. If the mode of the output is 2, the default scale factor is 1 regardless of whether the log is being taken. The scale is also 1 if there is relative normalization without taking logs. Otherwise, the scale factor for logarithms is 5000, +/-10000, or +/-50 for modes 1, 6, or 0; the scale for absolute linear normalizations is 25000, -50000, or -250 for modes 1, 6, or 0. Negative scaling is needed to fit absolute normalized data into the unsigned modes.

Field.name: ReverseContrast
Field.usage: Reverse contrast from input data by using negative scaling
Field.manpage: Reverse contrast from input data by using negative scaling. With positive scaling, the values produced by the program will have the same contrast polarity as the input, with density dark, but absolute normalization will produce negative numbers.

Field.name: IgnoreExposures
Field.usage: Ignore exposure data in image file when producing log output
Field.manpage: Use this option if you just want to take the logarithm of the input images without normalizing by exposure data in image file header.

Field.name: ExposureFile
Field.usage: File with an exposure value for each image
Field.manpage: File with an exposure value for each image, one per line. These can be either electron doses, or exposure times if the beam intensity was constant.

Field.name: TiltFile
Field.usage: File with tilt angles for using cosines as weights
Field.manpage: File with tilt angles, one per line. If this option is entered, the program will compute normalization factors by assuming that the exposures were inversely proportional to the cosine of the tilt angle, possibly raised to a power as specified by -power.

Field.name: CosinePowerInverse
Field.usage: Inverse of power applied to cosine of tilt angle
Field.manpage: When varying the exposure by the inverse of the cosine of the tilt angle, SerialEM has an option to moderate the amount of exposure change by taking this inverse to 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 or 1/5 power. Use this option to specify the selected power if normalization is being done with a tilt angle file.

Field.name: MinimumLogFactor
Field.usage: Minimum fraction of dynamic range to allow when taking log
Field.manpage: Minimum fraction of dynamic range to allow when taking the log. Before taking the log, small values will be truncated at this fraction times the difference between the maximum and minimum of the input file. The default is 0.001, the same value that is used in Tilt(1) to prevent small values from dominating the contrast range.

Field.name: ParameterFile
Field.usage: Read parameter entries from file
Field.manpage: Read parameter entries as keyword-value pairs from a parameter file.

Field.name: usage
Field.usage: Print help output
